claims.text: Neither is ever concatenated before scanning.
claims.why: The comment refers to something not present in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: author_vendor names the vendor that WROTE the material, so a council seat held by that same vendor is flagged self_review on every one of its turns.
claims.why: The self_review flag is defined in TurnRef but the logic that sets it is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Evidence citations: path + sha256 of the EXACT bytes shown. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without the digest the transcript records a citation nobody can reproduce.
claims.why: The method returns tuple of evidence_ref(path, (text or '').encode(...)) for each file, which includes the digest of the exact bytes.

claims.text: From spine.attempt.PatchArtifact -- the first intended input.
claims.why: The method accepts artifact and creates Evidence using getattr to access PatchArtifact-like attributes.

claims.text: changed_paths becomes the path channel; the diff itself is shown as one evidence file so the content channel scans it whole-file, per the floor's own contract.
claims.why: The method sets paths from artifact.changed_paths and files to ("PATCH.diff", diff).

claims.text: Read files off disk as evidence. Unreadable files are NAMED, never silently dropped -- a missing evidence file that reads as an empty one is a council reviewing something other than what it says it reviewed.
claims.why: The method catches OSError and appends '<<UNREADABLE: ...>>' text, so the file is named and not silently dropped.

claims.text: One assertion by one participant, VERBATIM.
claims.why: Claim dataclass fields include text (verbatim), verbatim, and parsed flag.

claims.text: checkable is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion. That is the council's entire product: a queue of checks for the gate to run.
claims.why: Claim has checkable bool and check string fields; no other logic in this chunk contradicts.

claims.text: A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own.
claims.why: Claim dataclass stores all fields regardless of checkable flag.

claims.text: The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing. There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object.
claims.why: CouncilRecord has advisory=True enforced in __post_init__, and no approve/reject fields exist.

claims.text: What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting.
claims.why: CouncilRecord has fields for claims, checkable_claims property, participants, turns, etc.

claims.text: Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision.
claims.why: __post_init__ raises ValueError if advisory is not True.

claims.text: The queue the gate can actually run.
claims.why: Property filters claims where c.checkable is True.

claims.text: "2 of 4 (2 distinct weight families)" -- never a bare fraction. "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same thing.
claims.why: Property returns string with responded, requested, and distinct_classes.

claims.text: Human rendering. The degraded flag sits ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS -- never in a footer, where a reader takes a two-vendor council for four.
claims.why: Degraded flag is printed inline with quorum line, not in footer.

claims.text: Split a response into claims, keeping every byte VERBATIM.
claims.why: Function returns Claim objects with verbatim text and parsed flag; for non-matching lines, it creates a single Claim with parsed=False.

claims.text: A vendor that ignores the format is NOT summarised and NOT dropped: its whole answer becomes one parsed=False claim. Summarising dissent is the failure this module exists to avoid, so the parser never paraphrases.
claims.why: When no lines match _CLAIM_RE, the function returns a single Claim with parsed=False containing the full content.

observations.what: from_patch_artifact uses getattr with default '' for many fields; if artifact is None or missing attributes, it may silently produce empty strings instead of raising an error.
from_files uses str(raw).replace('\\', '/') for name; this normalizes backslashes but may produce unexpected paths on Windows if raw is already a Path object.
CouncilRecord.__post_init__ checks self.advisory is True; if advisory is set to a truthy value like 1, the check passes, though the docstring says 'Always True and enforced'.
